I'm applying for the Lead Solutions Architect role.

I started at Webflow in support. I answered tickets, helped customers get unstuck, and learned what confuses people about our platform. That led to managing a team, which led to building an LMS to train new teammates, which led to using that same system to scale support to APAC.

Then the Marketplace team asked for help building a template submission system. I built it. I left Webflow for a while. They brought me back as a contractor to keep working on it. Then I rejoined full-time.

Along the way, I helped launch Webflow University 2.0. I learned how to explain complex things to different audiences—executives who want outcomes, developers who want APIs, designers who want to know how it works.

Now I build the systems that run our marketplace. The App Submission Form handles retries automatically and catches duplicates before they become problems. The Dashboard lets creators manage their templates, track analytics, and roll back changes when something goes wrong. The Validator checks projects against best practices—I used Rust for the heavy lifting because JavaScript was too slow for large projects.

These aren't prototypes. They're what the marketplace runs on.

Outside Webflow, I'm building AI-native tools. I'm learning what actually works with LLMs in production, not just in demos. As Webflow becomes an AI-native platform, that experience will matter.

I've worked with Webflow customers at every stage—when they're stuck, when they're learning, when they're building. I know what they need because I've been the one helping them get it.

This role is the synthesis of everything I've done here. I'm ready for it.
